summary: Raw memory, Buffer allocation, page allocation, volatile access, and memory primitives
lead: Raw-memory capabilities for explicit low-level work. `mem.slice<T>(ptr, count, owner)` creates a readonly zero-copy Slice over a canonical target layout, while `mem.withSliceMut<T>` scopes writable access to a callback; `mem.load/store<T>` use target-sized scalar descriptors, and `mem.alloc*` returns managed `Buffer`.
